claim_1.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum from the Montreal cohort (20 volunteers) after primary vaccination (day 0) showed that YF17D elicited neutralizing humoral immune responses (seroconversion), as summarized in Table S2.

sources.quote: Three volunteers (YF0014, 15, and 16), who were weak responders to the vaccine as measured by T cell proliferation, did not show a mixed Th1/Th2 profile; however, these individuals were still able to mount very good antibody responses (Table S2, available at http://www.jem.org/cgi/content/full/jem.20082292/DC1 ).

The volunteer recruitment and vaccination protocols for this study were approved by the research ethics committees of the Centre Hospitalier de l'Université de Montréal (Montreal cohort; 20 volunteers), the Faculty of Biology and Medicine of the University of Lausanne (Lausanne cohort; 13 volunteers), and Emory University (Emory Cohort; 10 volunteers). Each recruited subject received a single 0.5-ml subcutaneous injection of the Sanofi-Pasteur 17D-204 live-attenuated YF virus vaccine YF-VAX (Montreal and Emory cohorts) or Stamaril (Lausanne cohort).
YF17D-specific seroconversion and viremia were determined as described in Tables S2 and S5, respectively.

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of whole-blood RNA from 15 YF17D-vaccinated individuals in the Montreal cohort at primary vaccination (day 0) and days 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60 after primary vaccination (day 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60) showed significant modulation of 594 genes versus day 0, peaking at days 3 and 7, including up-regulation of TLR7, MYD88, IRF7, IFI27, IFI30, G1P2, G1P3, OAS1-3, C1QA, C1QB, C3AR1, SERPING1, CD86, CSF1R, MARCO, IFI16, KIR2DL3, KIR2DL4, PRF1, GNLY, GZMB, BANK1, CD19, IGJ, TNFRSF13B, and TNFRSF17l.

sources.quote: RNA samples obtained from whole blood of 15 YF17D-vaccinated individuals (from the Montreal cohort) on the day of vaccination (day 0) and at several time points after vaccination (day 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, and 60) were amplified and hybridized onto Illumina chips and analyzed.

Expression profiles of 594 genes (Supplemental document 1, available at http://www.jem.org/cgi/content/full/jem.20082292/DC1 ) were found to change significantly between day 0 and any time point after vaccination (with P < 0.05 and fold change less than −1.3 or >1.3). The peak of modulation of gene expression, as shown by heat map representation ( Fig. 1 a ) and principal component analysis ( Fig. 1 b ), primarily occurred at days 3 and 7 after vaccination, whereas a limited number of significant genes were modulated in response to vaccination at day 10 after vaccination or beyond.

Some Toll-like receptor (TLR)–associated genes (TLR7, MYD88, and IRF7) were also up-regulated, leading to the activation of the IFN pathway, as monitored by the induction of several IFN-induced genes (IFI27, IFI30, G1P2, G1P3, and OAS1-3; Fig. 3 a and Supplemental document 1). Components of the complement system (C1QA, C1QB, C3AR1, and SERPING1) were found to be up-regulated in blood cells early after vaccination ( Fig. 3 b ). A few macrophage/DC-associated genes were induced significantly by the vaccine, including CD86 (a marker of DC maturation), CSF1R, MARCO, and IFI16, which are expressed by cells of the monocyte-macrophage lineage ( Fig. 3 c ). NK cell–associated genes (KIR2DL3, KIR2DL4, PRF1, GNLY, and GZMB) were also up-regulated ( Fig. 3 d ). Genes associated with B cell activation (BANK1, CD19, IGJ, TNFRSF13B, and TNFRSF17l; Fig. 3 e ) were also modulated.

Each recruited subject received a single 0.5-ml subcutaneous injection of the Sanofi-Pasteur 17D-204 live-attenuated YF virus vaccine YF-VAX (Montreal and Emory cohorts) or Stamaril (Lausanne cohort). For the Montreal cohort, 50 ml of blood were drawn from each volunteer in sodium-heparinized Vacutainer tubes (BD) on the day of vaccination (day 0) and 3, 7, 10, 14, 28, 60, 90, 180, and 365 d thereafter. PBMCs were isolated from these samples using standard Ficoll-Paque Plus (GE Healthcare) density gradient centrifugation and cryopreserved in bovine serum + 10% DMSO in liquid nitrogen. At each time point, an additional 10 ml of blood was collected from each volunteer in PaxGene tubes (QIAGEN), for whole-blood RNA isolation.
